notes:
Summary: Ironwood is an EU-headquartered industrial cybersecurity platform building real-time secops assistants and embedding-based anomaly detection. They have strict data residency and retention rules for customer telemetry (EU-only), require audit logs retained for up to 7 years, and need KMS integration with their on-prem HSM and Azure Key Vault wrap (customer-managed keys).

Vendor Risk / SIG Intake: Risk team sent standard SIG and CAIQ; Ironwood expects full responses and wants mapped evidence for every control flagged as partial. They requested: SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary, SBOM for runtime components, and a completed CAIQ exported spreadsheet. SE is populating CAIQ draft (drive link). Risk notes: "If controls are not fully met, provide compensating controls and timelines."

Shared responsibility / Network controls: Key ask is explicit shared-responsibility matrix showing which plane (redwood control plane vs customer VPC) handles network egress, logging, backups, and key material. They insist on no shared internet egress from the customer VPC except via approved proxies. They want a template firewall ruleset and config for private endpoints.

KMS & Key Management: Requirement: Customer-managed keys, HSM-backed. They will not allow service-side key generation for models that process regulated telemetry. Need KMS integration guide and example KMS CSR flow. Also asked for crypto algorithm support (RSA-2048, RSA-3072, AES-GCM) and key rotation SLA.

Audit logging & SIEM: Mandatory: real-time audit stream to their SIEM (S3 + Kinesis or syslog) with tamper-evident write-once storage for selected logs. Retention 7 years for security-critical logs. Must provide token-level attribution in logs and mapping of user/email -> token. They asked how we store API tokens and whether token hashes are reversible.

Data residency & retention: Data must be stored and processed only in EU regions. Backup snapshots must be region-restricted. Deletion/retention policy needs displayable proof for audits (delete flows, WORM schedules). Legal asked for subprocessors list and data flow diagram.

Compliance artifacts requested: SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, penetration test executive summary, privacy impact assessment, subprocessors list, export-controlled software declarations. They gave a 10-business-day SLA to return the SIG with attachments.

POC scope / Milestones: 1) Access to isolated VPC environment + test account (week 1), 2) KMS integration trial with sample keys (week 2), 3) Live ingestion of non-production telemetry + audit stream to SIEM (week 3), 4) Performance/runbook review and final security sign-off (week 4). SE already provisioned a staging cluster for step 1.

Quotes / verbatim: "We cannot accept keys held by vendors for regulated telemetry." - Head of InfoSec. "Need clear SLA for key rotation and emergency key revocation." - CTO.

- Provide a shared-responsibility matrix doc and example firewall ruleset for customer VPC peering.
